title: How to Use Lifetime Income Products (SPIAs, DIA annuities)
description: Buying a personal pension to guarantee you never run out of money.
content:
The decline of corporate pensions has left retirees managing their own longevity risk. If you live to 105, will your 401(k) last? Lifetime Income Products—specifically Single Premium Immediate Annuities (SPIAs) and Deferred Income Annuities (DIAs)—allow you to transfer this risk to an insurance company. You trade a lump sum of cash for a guaranteed monthly paycheck for life. While 'Annuity' is often a dirty word due to high fees on complex products, simple income annuities are highly efficient tools for risk-averse retirees.

Key Takeaways

  • Mortality Credits: The unique benefit of annuities. The insurance company pools money. Those who die early subsidize those who live long. If you live to 95, you get a return that no bond portfolio can match.
  • SPIA (Immediate): You pay $100k now, you get ~$600/month starting next month for life. It acts like an instant pension.
  • DIA (Deferred): You pay $100k now at age 60, and it starts paying ~$1,200/month at age 80. This is 'Longevity Insurance' for your old age.
  • The 'Safety Floor': Use annuities to cover your fixed expenses (housing/food) that Social Security doesn't cover. Keep the rest of your portfolio in stocks for inflation protection.

Why It Matters (US Context)

Interest rates drive annuity payouts. Buying an annuity when interest rates are 5% locks in a much higher lifetime income than buying when rates are 1%. High-rate environments are the best time to buy.

Annuity Types Explained

Stick to the simple ones.

1. SPIA (Single Premium Immediate Annuity)

Structure: Simple transaction. Cash for Income.
Pros: Zero ambiguity. High cash flow.
Cons: Loss of principal (usually). If you die tomorrow, the money is gone (unless you buy 'Period Certain' protection).

2. QLAC (Qualified Longevity Annuity Contract)

Structure: A DIA bought inside an IRA/401k.
Pros: You can put up to $200k (2025). It is exempt from RMDs until age 85. It lowers your taxes today and guarantees income at 85.

3. Variable / Indexed Annuities (Avoid)

Structure: Complex investment products with insurance wrappers.
Cons: High fees (2-3%), surrender charges, capped returns. Usually sold by commission-hungry agents. Stick to SPIAs/DIAs.

Buying Strategy

  1. Laddering: Don't buy one big annuity. Buy smaller ones over time (e.g., $50k at age 65, $50k at 70). This hedges interest rate risk.
  2. Inflation Check: Standard annuities pay a fixed dollar amount. Inflation eats this. Keep a separate stock portfolio to handle inflation, or buy a COLA rider (expensive).
  3. Carrier Safety: You are betting the insurance company will exist in 30 years. Only buy from A++ rated carriers. State Guaranty funds offer some protection ($250k limit usually), but don't rely on it.
  4. The 'Sleep' Test: If the stock market keeps you awake, an annuity buys peace. The mathematical 'loss' of upside is the price of sleep.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I get my money back?

With a SPIA, generally No. It is an irrevocable contract. You traded liquidity for income. Do not put more than 30-40% of your net worth in annuities.

Is it taxable?

If bought with IRA money (Qualified), the whole check is taxable income. If bought with Cash (Non-Qualified), only the earnings portion is taxed.

What about my heirs?

Annuities are for you. Stocks are for heirs. If leaving a legacy is the goal, don't buy an annuity. If not running out of money is the goal, buy one.
